scope: edi is 0 at the push point and the ring-calculation path never runs; the observed ring index is 31, suggesting a sequence-window issue
what_this_shows: the ring-address computation at 0x4722B0..0x4722C0 is NEVER executed for our snapshots - that branch is not taken
the value pushed as arg3 is literally zero, and the client keeps 31 in [ebx+0xA8DC] (the index the ring branch would mask and multiply by 0x3BBC)

so the client is in the 'no valid snapshot slot' path, and the index it holds (31) is suspicious: if the ring has a small power-of-two size, an out-of-window sequence number would make the slot invalid
the_new_hypothesis: we send snapshots with --snapshot-seq 1000, an arbitrary large sequence number
a real server sends a small, incrementing sequence; the client masks it into its snapshot ring (0x3BBC stride) and the ring index observed (31) is consistent with a small modulo window
a sequence number far outside the window would make every snapshot land on an invalid slot - which is exactly the NULL history we measure
next_test: re-run with --snapshot-seq 1 (and a short interval) and check whether 0x4722C0 (RingCalc) now fires and arg3 becomes non-zero
if it does, the sequence window is the blocker and the whole content path opens up; if not, the blocker is earlier in the load flow
